previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for fever and pyuria. She had a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs and recent sepsis. On admission, she had leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and cellulitis of the left stump. Urine culture grew ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, and tissue cultures from a stump revision grew ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and E. coli. An MRI was inconclusive for osteomyelitis, but due to clinical concern, she underwent stump revision and was started on IV tigecycline. Her kidney function improved with fluids, and she completed a course of vancomycin for soft tissue infection. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. She was discharged home on a six-week course of IV tigecycline with follow-up in Infectious Disease, Vascular Surgery, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ w/PMHx DM s/p b/l BKAs, being treated for 6 weeks for 
polymicrobial presumed left stump osteomyelitis vs myositis, 
admitted for nausea, vomiting, and copious diarrhea.

Active Issues:
.
# Diarrhea 
On presentation, the patient reported two days of worsening 
diarrhea, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Although the 
patient has had episodes of c.diff diarrhea previously, the 
patient's tigecycline was provisionally held on the 
recommendation of ID, and PO vancomycin was given. The morning 
following admission, the patient stated that her nausea and 
vomiting remitted, she tolerated a regular diet. The degree of 
her diarrhea also diminished significantly.  Given the time 
course of stopping the tigecycline and her remission of 
symptoms, this was likely a side effect of the tigecycline.
.  
# Left BKA Osteo:
On admission to the hospital, the patient was transitioned from 
IV tigecycline to IV Vancomycin/Meropenem in order to avoid 
potential side effects of the tigecycline. The patient tolerated 
the change well. The morning after admission, the patient was 
evaluated by the vascular surgery service, who debrided her left 
BKA ulcer; however, the extent of the ulcer is such that it will 
require an AKA for definitive management. The patient was 
initially apprehensive about this decision, but voiced 
understanding that this is the only curative option for the 
infection, and agreed to set a date for the surgery within two 
weeks. For the interim period between presentation and the 
surgery, the patient was started on Bactrim. The patient will 
follow up in ___ clinic in between discharge and surgery.
.  
# UTI: 
The patient has a history of UTI and U/A was positive on this 
admission. Patient has had klebsiella and E. Coli UTI in the 
past.  During the ___ hospital stay, the IV 
Vancomycin/Meropenem combination was thought to cover the most 
likely pathogens, and the patient was asymptomatic when 
discharged on PO Bactrim.  Although final urine culture was 
pending at the time of discharge, the patient's regimen can be 
further tailored if necessary in several days at ___ clinic.
.  
Chronic Issues:
.  
# Diabetes  
- The patient was maintained on her home regimen of lantus and 
humalog. There was no significant change in her disease course 
during this admission, and the patient was discharged with an 
additional copy of the sliding scale and its accompanying 
literature.
.
